text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- About 400 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) militants set fire to a cell where PKK confessors are held in a prison in the southeastern city of Diyarbakir. Eight prisoners died.
- State Minister Ufuk Soylemez, who held meetings with International Monetary Fund and World Bank officials in the United States, says there will be no new stand-by deal.
- Top traditional Turkish music singer, Zeki Muren, dies of a heart attack.
- Car producer TOFAS halts production for a fortnight due to a 40 percent narrowing in the car sales market.
- The directorate of religious affairs says there is great ignorance about religion in Turkey.
- Court bans the broadcasting of a news programme revealing sexual abuse of pupils by lecturers in a private Islamist boarding school.
- Turkey has made exports worth $16 billion and imports worth $27.1 billion in the last eight months.
- The murderer of the environment is the ministry of environment itself after it gave a clean bill of health to three thermal power plants notorious for high pollution levels.
- Turkish armed forces operations against Kurdish rebels intensify. The chief of staff and the armed forces commander are in the region.
